messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected from model-runtime cluster 'infer-prod' starting 2026-03-14T01:12:25Z. 5m error rate 12% (baseline ~0.2%). Top error patterns: OOM / segfaults in runtime. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/infer-prod/dashboard (PD-6789 created)

john: ack — I'm oncall. Paging @lee and @ankita. Which customers are impacted?

PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by lee (lee).

lee: looking at pod logs now. seeing repeated OOM kills on node gpu-3 and a segfault in the runtime process. tail: 
```
Mar 14 01:10:54 gpu-3 model-runtime[2345]: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 13.6 GiB already allocated)
Mar 14 01:10:54 gpu-3 kernel: [12345.678] Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (model-runtime) score 987
Mar 14 01:10:55 gpu-3 model-runtime[2345]: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

lee: preliminary hypothesis: combination of increased QPS + MAX_BATCH_SIZE growth caused KV-cache and attention buffers to blow past GPU memory on the latest runtime build. possible memory regression in attention kernel.

ankita: I can roll back yesterday's kernel/attention patch. immediate mitigations we should do now:
1) Reduce MAX_BATCH_SIZE to 8
2) Disable KV cache for stateless/generic endpoints
3) Route high-throughput customers to a smaller quantized variant (redwood/gptq-7b) as fallback
4) Cordon & drain gpu-3 to stop repeated restarts

support-bot: affected customers flagged: cust-alpha (timeouts), cust-beta (5xx spike), several smaller customers. sample request ids seen failing: req_8a1, req_8a2, req_9f3. public endpoints show elevated p95 latency and errors.

john: do the mitigations. lee — cordon/drain and restart pods. ankita — prepare rollback and canary. product-ops, prepare status page.

lee: running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-3
kubectl drain gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deploy/model-runtime --replicas=10 --namespace=infer-prod
kubectl apply -f /configs/runtime-hotfix.yaml
```

lee: also temporarily set ENV MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 and RUNTIME_KV_CACHE=false via configmap to push quick change. restarting 6 pods.

product-ops: drafting status: "We are investigating increased error rates impacting text generation. Engineering is mitigating; a subset of customers may experience 5xx/timeouts. Updates every 15 minutes." ETA 30m for initial mitigation message.

lee: after hotfix rollout — 5xx dropped from 12% -> ~1.8% over last 5m. no new segfaults on replaced pods. still seeing older pods churn on gpu-3.

ankita: started rollback build for attention kernel patch. if rollback fails we keep fallback routing to quantized variant. building artifact now.

ankita: build succeeded. deploying rollback via canary to model-runtime-1 (10% -> 50% -> 100%).

ankita: canary results: stable, no OOMs in canary pods for 20m. increasing to 50%.

support-bot: notified top-10 affected customers with interim mitigation note.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: STATUS UPDATE: mitigating -> resolved_degraded. 5xx returned to near-baseline after config changes and rollback canary. Postmortem required. Postmortem doc created: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/PD-6789-postmortem

john: handing off to ankita to own postmortem + RCA; lee stays on for follow-ups and ticket creation.

lee: action items I'm making tickets for:
- SRE-204: Add memory pressure alert (GPU memory consumption > 85% for 2m)
- SRE-205: Add runtime OOM/segfault log parser + linked trace IDs
- ENG-312: Run load test with MAX_BATCH_SIZE=12 and seq_len 2048 under stress harness
- ENG-313: Revert attention kernel patch and run GPU regression tests before re-landing

product-ops: status page published: "Degraded performance between 01:10 - 02:05 UTC. Errors reduced; we continue root cause analysis and will share final report."

support-bot: customers contacted and provided mitigation steps and ETA for final report.

ankita: postmortem summary draft: suspected memory leak in attention kernel when sequence_len>2048 under mixed-precision + KV cache enabled. Root cause: edge-case buffer growth combined with new kernel allocator behavior. Immediate fix: rollback patch + cap MAX_BATCH_SIZE + cap seq_len to 2048. Follow-up: add regression test, improve allocators.

lee: added runtime config change: cap seq_len = 2048 and enforced MAX_BATCH_SIZE <= 12 for now. will monitor.

john: good work. follow-up postmortem meeting scheduled for 2026-03-16T14:00:00Z UTC. Ankita to lead. Closing the incident thread when postmortem doc is finalized.

ankita: created ENG ticket ENG-314 for kernel regression test and linked postmortem: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/PD-6789-postmortem (doc created).

lee: leaving final note: suspected leak confirmed on internal repro; patch candidate posted to PR #4627.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved at 2026-03-14T02:07:30Z (thread closed).

john: thanks all.
